name: Centralia
tax_rate: 2% (additional special lodging tax dedicated to tourism)
deadline_pattern: Applications open late summer/fall, due to City Clerk in fall (Sept 19, 2025 for 2026; Nov 23, 2026 for 2027); LTAC reviews in late fall, Council approves in December/January
contact: Bret Brodersen, Finance Director, bbrodersen@cityofcentralia.com, 360-330-7671; City Clerk's office 360-330-7670
notes: For 2026 the city approved $247,567 in lodging tax awards (about $96,000 available above Fox Theatre and event center debt payments) to seven nonprofit applicants after presentations to LTAC on Dec 3, 2025; the 2027 application is posted with a Nov 23, 2026 noon deadline.

presentation.pattern: Applicants presented to the LTAC at its evaluation meeting in early December (Dec 3, 2025 for the 2026 cycle); expect a similar meeting in December 2026 for 2027 requests

meeting_schedule: LTAC meets two to three times per year, typically fall and early December

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Application (City of Centralia)
funding_docs.summary: Application for the city's 2% special lodging tax grants, due Nov 23, 2026 at noon; nonprofits and government agencies eligible, with preference for projects that increase overnight stays. No pool or cap stated.

funding_docs.title: Centralia City Council approves nearly $250K in lodging tax funding (Jan 2026 award list)
funding_docs.summary: Council unanimously approved LTAC's recommendation of $247,567 against $345,721 requested: $84,600 event center bond debt, $66,967 Fox Theatre loan, and grants led by Downtown Centralia Festivals Association ($33,000) and Centralia Downtown Association ($28,000).

funding_docs.title: City of Centralia accepting applications for 2026 hotel/motel lodging tax grants (Aug 2025 notice)
funding_docs.summary: Prior-cycle call for applications with a Sept 19, 2025 noon deadline; confirms the annual pattern and nonprofit/government eligibility.

pool_note: 2026: $247,567 available and approved; $84,600 event center bond debt and $66,967 Fox Theatre loan are standing commitments, leaving $96,000 awarded across seven outside nonprofit applicants.

name: Aberdeen
deadline_pattern: Applications open early October, due first week of November at 4:00 p.m.; LTAC hears presentations and recommends in December; contracts issued in January
contact: Stacie Barnum, Parks and Recreation Director, sbarnum@aberdeenwa.gov, 360-537-3229; Katy Williamsen, Finance Director, kwilliamsen@aberdeenwa.gov, 360-537-3201
notes: The 2026 cycle (apps due Nov 6, 2025) budgeted $90,000 for projects against $161,200 requested, with each applicant given a 3-minute presentation at the Dec 9, 2025 LTAC meeting; the 2027 packet was not yet found online so dates shown are from the prior cycle.

presentation.pattern: Each applicant gives a 3-minute presentation at the December LTAC meeting (5:30 p.m., City Hall 3rd floor council chambers)

meeting_schedule: One to three times per year, mainly a December review meeting at 5:30 p.m., Aberdeen City Hall, 200 E Market St

funding_docs.title: 2026 Lodging Tax Fund Application Packet (Aberdeen Parks and Recreation)
funding_docs.summary: Guidelines for the 2% lodging tax grants: nonprofit or government applicants, 25% cash or in-kind match, reimbursement-only contracts, itemized budget and board list required, final report due within 3 weeks of the event.

funding_docs.title: 2026 LTAC Grant Application (fillable) with timeline
funding_docs.summary: Sets the cycle: applications open Oct 3, 2025, due Nov 6, 2025 at 4 p.m., decisions in December, contracts in January for a Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026 contract period; eligible uses are marketing, events and tourism facilities.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Committee agenda, Dec 9, 2025 (funding request table)
funding_docs.summary: Lists 14 requests totaling $161,200 against $90,000 budgeted for projects and an estimated $409,474 fund balance; largest asks were Pacific NW Music Project $30,000, City traffic control $20,000 and ghOST Project $20,000, each with a 3-minute presentation.

funding_docs.title: Aberdeen seeks LTAC members (Daily World, Apr 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Reports the prior round awarded $110,000 to 11 applicants for festivals, beautification and art.

pool_note: 2026: LTAC agenda showed $90,000 budgeted for projects (fund balance about $409,474) against $161,200 requested, including $50,000 of city Parks and traffic/decoration requests, so the outside share is an estimate at or below $90,000; the prior round awarded $110,000 to 11 applicants.

name: Longview
notes: No city lodging tax grant application, LTAC page or roster was found on mylongview.com or in news coverage; the city appears not to run an open application process, and the regional lodging tax grants for Longview-area events are run by Cowlitz County Tourism.

alternatives.administrator: Cowlitz County Tourism Department (LTAC recommends, Board of County Commissioners approves)
alternatives.funds: County hotel/motel lodging tax under RCW 67.28; reimbursement-based, 25% match required
alternatives.eligibility: Public agencies and nonprofits (501c3/501c6, chambers, museums, historical societies) running events that draw visitors from beyond 50 miles and generate hotel stays
alternatives.deadline_pattern: Notice late September, applications due first week of November at 4:30 p.m., awards announced by Dec 31 for the following calendar year
alternatives.contact: Dawn Smith, Tourism Coordinator, smithd@cowlitzwa.gov, 360-577-3137; Kim Bowcutt, Tourism Director
alternatives.notes: Office is at 1900 7th Avenue, Longview; the 2025 packet is the most recent one found, so confirm the 2027 cycle dates.

funding_docs.title: Cowlitz County Tourism Grant Application for 2025 Funds
funding_docs.summary: County lodging tax grant guidelines: public agencies and nonprofits, events drawing visitors from beyond 50 miles, 25% match, reimbursement basis, applications due Nov 6, 2024; no total pool stated. No City of Longview lodging tax allocation document was found.

pool_note: No City of Longview lodging tax budget or allocation document was found, so neither the revenue nor any committed uses could be confirmed.

name: Camas
deadline_pattern: Window opens late March and closes early May (May 6, 2024; May 9, 2025) for same-year funding; LTAC reviews at a spring meeting and Council confirms
contact: Carrie Davis, Executive Assistant to the Mayor and City Administrator, Administration@CityofCamas.us, 360-834-6864; City Clerk's Office 360-817-1591
notes: Camas runs a small spring application window funded by a 2% lodging tax (about $30,000 awarded in 2024) and asks applicants to be available in person or via Zoom at the LTAC review meeting; the 2026 window was not found online so the 2025 dates are shown.

presentation.pattern: Applicants are asked to be available at the LTAC review meeting (mid/late May, Council Chambers) to answer questions, in person or via Zoom; attendance is welcomed, not mandatory

meeting_schedule: Annually, usually early spring to review applications; hybrid Zoom/in person at City Hall, 616 NE 4th Ave

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Funds Availability (City of Camas program overview)
funding_docs.summary: Describes the 2% lodging tax program: government and nonprofit applicants, permitted uses under RCW 67.28, priority for overnight stays, outside promotion, economic benefit and partnerships; 2025 window Mar 24 to May 9 with Council consensus and a municipal services contract. No pool stated.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Application Window Opens 3/25/24
funding_docs.summary: 2024 cycle notice: applications due May 6, 2024 at 5 p.m., LTAC review meeting May 21, 2024 in Council Chambers.

funding_docs.title: Camas awards $30K from lodging taxes (Camas-Washougal Post-Record, June 2024)
funding_docs.summary: Reports about $30,000 in 2024 lodging tax awards approved by Council on LTAC's recommendation; the article could not be opened to list individual recipients.

pool_note: 2024: about $30,000 awarded to outside applicants from the 2% lodging tax per the Post-Record; total annual revenue was not published.

name: Winthrop
notes: Winthrop Municipal Code 2.52 creates an LTAC that recommends uses of the town's lodging tax, but the funds are budgeted for town marketing through a contracted marketing committee rather than an open grant round, and no application form or deadline was found.
meeting_schedule: LTAC must meet at least quarterly per WMC 2.52

alternatives.funds: County hotel/motel tax collected on lodging outside town limits, including the Methow Valley
alternatives.eligibility: Nonprofits and public agencies promoting tourism in Okanogan County
alternatives.notes: Methow Valley organizations such as Methow Trails have received county lodging tax funds; details were not verified in this pass.

alternatives.administrator: Town of Winthrop via its contracted marketing program and LTAC
alternatives.funds: About $85,000 per year budgeted from the 3% hotel/motel tax (2012 figure) for marketing only
alternatives.eligibility: Not an open grant; event promotion requests go to the town council or LTAC directly
alternatives.notes: Figure is from a 2012 article and should be refreshed.

funding_docs.title: Winthrop Municipal Code Chapter 2.52, Lodging Tax Advisory Committee
funding_docs.summary: Creates a 5 to 8 member LTAC (two lodging tax collectors, two business owners, a Chamber board member, an elected chair) that recommends uses of lodging tax funds to Council and monitors contracted tourism marketing; no grant process or allocation amounts.

funding_docs.title: Winthrop's Three Percent Tax (Methow Grist, Aug 2012)
funding_docs.summary: Reports the town's 3% hotel-motel tax of roughly $85,000 per year is budgeted for marketing only and overseen by a seven-member marketing committee; figures are dated.

pool_note: 2012 estimate: roughly $85,000 a year from the 3% tax, all budgeted to the town's contracted marketing program with no open grant round; current revenue not found.

name: Lynden
deadline_pattern: Applications open June 30 and are due first week of August; LTAC reviews mid-September; Council approves in November; contracts in December
notes: Lynden runs one annual round (2027 apps were due Aug 7, 2026 and reviewed Sept 15, 2026) on a reimbursement basis, with no formal presentation required.

presentation.pattern: No formal presentation; applicants may attend the September LTAC review meeting and may be asked questions

meeting_schedule: Once a year in late summer (Sept 15, 2026), date set by the Chair

funding_docs.title: Lynden Lodging Tax Advisory Committee program page and 2027 application timeline
funding_docs.summary: One project per application, full program budget required, reimbursement only, eligible uses are tourism promotion and tourism facilities; applications open June 30, due Aug 7, 2026, LTAC review Sept 15, Council approval November, reports due Jan 31. No pool or cap stated.

funding_docs.title: Lynden City Council minutes, Mar 17, 2025 (LTAC appointments)
funding_docs.summary: Confirms the five-member LTAC appointments through Dec 31, 2025 and that LTAC recommendations feed the annual budget; no dollar amounts.

pool_note: Lynden publishes the application timeline but no lodging tax revenue, pool or award list was found.

name: Blaine
deadline_pattern: Applications due by email around the end of August / first business day of September (Sept 1, 2025 for 2026; Aug 31, 2026 for 2027); BTAC recommends in October, Council approves in November
contact: Alex Wenger, AICP, Community Development Services Director, awenger@cityofblaine.com, 360-332-8311 ext. 2001
notes: Blaine's Tourism Advisory Committee (BTAC) awards roughly $80,000 to $83,000 a year in reimbursable event grants from lodging tax, prefers multi-day events, and the 2027 application closed Aug 31, 2026.

presentation.pattern: Application packet does not require a presentation; BTAC reviews written applications at its fall meeting and recommends to Council

meeting_schedule: Quarterly, generally the 2nd Tuesday of the month at 8:30 a.m., Blaine City Hall

funding_docs.title: 2027 BTAC Grant Proposal Application (City of Blaine)
funding_docs.summary: Due Aug 31, 2026 by email; reimbursable grants only, preference for multi-day events tied to the Blaine by the Sea theme and 2019 Tourism Plan, applicants must report overnight stays and 50-mile visitors and show a path off lodging tax reliance. No pool or cap stated.

funding_docs.title: Blaine City Council approves tourism budget (The Northern Light, Nov 2024)
funding_docs.summary: Council approved $206,400 in tourism spending including $83,000 in event grants (vs $80,000 in 2024): largest were Old Fashioned Fourth of July $24,000, Blaine Harbor Music Festival $10,000 and Scottish Gathering $10,000, with $50,000 each for Welcome Center lease and management.

funding_docs.title: Blaine Tourism Advisory Committee page (2026 grant cycle notice)
funding_docs.summary: States BTAC reviews the hotel/motel tax budget and recommends grants; 2026 applications were due Sept 1, 2025 to Alex Wenger.

pool_note: 2025: $206,400 total tourism spending approved from lodging tax; Welcome Center lease and management ($100,000), events costs, marketing and staff absorb the rest, leaving $83,000 awarded across 11 event grants (seven routed through the Chamber/parks district).

name: Liberty Lake

notes: Liberty Lake awards competitive, reimbursement-based Tourism Fund grants with applications due in early December; 2024 requests totaled $80,550 across six applicants, and the 2026 or 2027 application was not found online so the 2025 cycle dates are shown.

members.name: Kyle Dixon
members.affiliation: City of Liberty Lake Finance Director

presentation.pattern: LTAC holds a special review meeting in spring (Apr 30, 2024, 1:00 p.m., City Hall council chambers); written public comment accepted; presentation requirement not stated

meeting_schedule: As needed; typically a late-summer meeting to release the application and a spring special meeting to review requests

funding_docs.title: 2025 Lodging Tax Grant Application and Guidelines (City of Liberty Lake)
funding_docs.summary: Competitive, reimbursement-based grants from the 2% Tourism Fund, due Dec 5, 2024 at 5 p.m.; eligible uses are tourism promotion, event marketing and tourism facilities; applicants must estimate room nights and show marketing to Liberty Lake lodging. No pool or cap stated.

funding_docs.title: LTAC special meeting agenda packet, Apr 30, 2024 (2024 funding requests)
funding_docs.summary: Six 2024 requests totaling $80,550: HUB Sports Center $15,000, Centennial Rotary $20,000, TAC at the Lake $20,000, Winter Glow Spectacular $20,000, two Kiwanis events $5,550 combined; includes Aug 2023 minutes approving the application release.

funding_docs.title: 2023 Tourism Promotion Funding notice and application
funding_docs.summary: Prior-cycle notice (due Dec 2, 2022) confirming the early-December pattern, 2% tax source and LTAC-recommends, Council-decides process.

name: Stevenson
deadline_pattern: Tourism promotion proposals due mid-October at 4:00 p.m. (Oct 13, 2025 for 2026; Oct 12, 2026 for 2027); Tourism Advisory Committee recommends, Council approves in December/January
contact: Ben Shumaker, City of Stevenson (TAC staff), 509-427-5970, 7121 E. Loop Road, Stevenson, WA 98648
notes: Stevenson's Tourism Advisory Committee (TAC) takes online applications in four categories each fall from a Tourism Promotion fund with a roughly $1.6M balance; the 2027 round closed Oct 12, 2026 and a late 2026 Kite & Wing Festival request was still approved in January 2026.

presentation.pattern: Not stated; TAC meets at least once a year after the October deadline to score proposals and recommend awards to Council

meeting_schedule: At least once a year, after the mid-October proposal deadline; see the TAC & Tourism Calendar on the city site

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Application Information and Guidelines (Apply for TAC Funding)
funding_docs.summary: Online portal with four funding categories; 2027 proposals due Oct 12, 2026; links a 2027 TAC and Tourism Calendar. No pool or cap stated on the page.

funding_docs.title: Stevenson City Council agenda packet, Jan 15, 2026 (TAC appointments and Kite & Wing Festival award)
funding_docs.summary: Shows the Tourism Promotion Fund (Fund 103) ending 2025 at about $1.61M, a $10,000 final TAC 2025 contract payment, TAC's unanimous $3,000 recommendation for the 2026 Bridge of the Gods Kite & Wing Festival, and the Oct 13, 2025 proposal deadline for 2026.

funding_docs.title: City of Stevenson 2024 Adopted Budget Book
funding_docs.summary: Adopted budget containing the Tourism Promotion and Development Fund appropriations; not opened in this pass, so amounts are unconfirmed.
